title: Separate production from staging
goal: Step 1 of #38: production gets its own app database, files bucket, file index and Cloudflare token, so a lawyer's case files never sit beside test data and a migration on dev is not live in production. Two app databases (user: 'separating now is good, 2 dbs, branch-based scoping in Neon'); the rest as planned in #38.
for_whom: The first practising lawyers who sign up (their confidential case files), and us building and testing without touching their data.

done_check.check: A new Neon project sllaw-prod in Singapore (aws-ap-southeast-1) with database `app`; every migration applied; its schema matches staging's (Neon compare_database_schema shows no difference).

A private R2 bucket for production files (unsigned GET refused), CORS allowing PUT from https://sllaw.vercel.app only; a production Cloudflare token scoped to that bucket and Workers AI. The staging bucket sllaw-files no longer allows sllaw.vercel.app.
A Zilliz collection for production files with the same schema and indexes as `files`; the collection name comes from an env variable (default `files`), so staging is unchanged.

Vercel Production variables point at the production database, bucket, collection and token; Development and Preview still point at staging. The law corpus (ETL_DATABASE_URL, law bucket, Zilliz `chunks`) stays shared and read-only.

Clerk (one shared instance) has a webhook endpoint for each environment: production at sllaw.vercel.app, staging at a fixed address (the `staging` branch's preview alias, through Vercel's automation bypass). A new sign-up appears as a user and workspace in both databases within a minute.

In a headed browser on sllaw.vercel.app: sign in, create a case, upload a text PDF (Ready), ask a question; the answer cites a law section and the file. The rows are in sllaw-prod only (staging's counts unchanged), the file in the production bucket, its vectors in the production collection. The same steps on local dev land in staging only.

Guards and map: `.claude/agent-db.json` names sllaw-prod; the guard asks before SQL or migrations against sllaw-prod and refuses running the app, evals or migrations from a brief worktree pointing at it, with cases in test_guard.py. CLAUDE.md map and rules, app/CLAUDE.md (env), docs/APP.md and .env.example say how it is now; #38 step 1 ticked.

scenarios.steps: A lawyer signs up on sllaw.vercel.app, creates a case, uploads a lease agreement and asks whether the landlord can evict without notice.
scenarios.expect: The file reads Ready, the answer cites the Act's section and the lease page; everything they made lives only in the production database, bucket and collection.

scenarios.steps: We upload a test file and chat on local dev (or a preview).
scenarios.expect: Nothing appears in production: a search in a production case never finds the test file, and production's file and chat counts don't change.

scenarios.steps: An agent runs a new migration on its agent/<slug> branch and on staging.
scenarios.expect: Production's schema is unchanged until the migration is run against sllaw-prod, and the guard asks first.

out_of_scope: A Clerk production instance and a custom domain (no domain bought yet; Clerk stays shared).
Corpus releases with stable chunk ids (#38 step 2) and pgvector replacing Zilliz (#38 step 3).
A Neon branch per PR preview (user: no).
Nightly backups to R2 (Neon's own restore window only).
Copying today's test users, cases or chats into production: it starts empty.
A separate AI Gateway key for production (it signs in through the Vercel project; usage_events records spend per environment).

decisions.note: Production is a new Neon project sllaw-prod in Singapore; today's sllaw-app becomes staging and stays in us-east-1; agent/<slug> branches stay off staging (user).
Only the app database splits; the corpus (sllaw-etl, kb) is already separate and stays shared, read-only (user).
No domain yet (neethi.ai is registered by someone else; neethilaw.com / neethiai.com are $12/yr, not bought). Clerk stays one shared instance, with a webhook endpoint per environment (user).
Previews use staging, no branch per PR (user). Production gets its own Cloudflare token; AI Gateway as is (user).
Parked (user): split production from dev later, once there is a solid product to release. Reopen from this brief and #38.
